ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: If the graph of the function $y=kx+b$ is shown in the figure, what is the solution set of the inequality $kx+b>0$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} From the graph, we can determine that the function $y=kx+b$ intersects the x-axis at $(2,0)$. Since $y$ decreases as $x$ increases, \\
$\therefore$ the solution set of the inequality $kx+b>0$ is $\boxed{x<2}$.

The position where the straight line intersects the x-axis is marked at x=2; on the left side of the intersection point, the straight line is above the x-axis, and on the right side of the intersection point, the straight line is below the x-axis.
